quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: Can pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
Can pass if you know the road ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means passing is not allowed. You must follow all regulatory signs.

questions.question: When driving in a travel lane:

options.text: You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop to look up an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: When someone is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait for clear road ahead and slowly reduce your speed to let them pass.

questions.explanation: Move to the right if possible. If not, wait for clear road ahead and slowly reduce speed. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit.

questions.question: If you drive in foggy weather:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back into your eyes and lower visibility. Turn on headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: In Washington State, an adult over 21 is legally drunk at a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: Adults over 21 can be arrested at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. Drivers under 21 can be arrested at 0.02 percent or higher.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach.

questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Increase your distance from other vehicles on slippery roads. Your car takes longer to stop in these conditions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two one-way paths. Stay on the right.

questions.question: What can you do with a shared center lane on a two-way road?

options.text: Use it to pass other vehicles.
Use it as a regular driving lane during rush hour.
Drive in it as long as you are turning left.
Drive in it for no more than 300 feet before turning left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive in it for no more than 300 feet before turning left.
questions.explanation: A shared center lane is only for left turns. You can use it for up to 300 feet. Do not use it to pass or travel long distances.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and slide on a thin layer of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a winding road with three or more curves ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Do all three things.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles that have flashing lights or sirens on.

questions.question: What is a speed restriction sign?

options.text: You can ignore it in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn signs show a recommended speed for that area. Even if you feel safe driving faster in good weather, slow down in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Gets broken down more quickly by your body.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your body, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes more driving errors.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the right air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on a thin layer of water. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights at an intersection are out due to a power outage?

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and go through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see. Headlights from other cars can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can get all the way across the tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can get all the way across the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before you drive onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at or near railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does a steady red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop. Do not go straight ahead.
Stop, look for danger, then cross.
Slow down and yield to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop. Do not go straight ahead.
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop completely. Wait until the light turns green and there is no crossing traffic before you move forward.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn immediately since you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When making a left turn with approaching traffic, wait for that traffic to pass before you turn. If the light is green and no other car is ahead of you turning left, you may move into the intersection to prepare for your turn.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly while you check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and merge at the same speed as traffic. Always yield to other traffic when entering.
